title: fix(update): a pnpm update no longer fails after activating when the updater itself was installed by an update
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on a pnpm install, the second update between two releases that both contain this fix-line ends `update-recovery-pending` (exit 1), even though the new version is installed and the Gateway serves it. Afterwards, every further update is refused with "Update <run> has unfinished recovery; reconcile it before starting another update."

## User Impact

User impact: once the updater running the update contains this change, pnpm updates between OpenClaw versions end `ok`, and the run is recorded `succeeded`. npm installs were not affected and are unchanged.

What changes nothing: a pnpm install whose updater is already a release without this change still hits the failure on its own next update, because the installed updater cannot be patched. Users who already hit it on an unfixed build stay blocked, and this PR does not change that. In a real cell, after the failed B → C, every later `openclaw update` (to F1, then F2) was refused within 2 s with "Update <id> has unfinished recovery … It belongs to the installation at <the removed B store path>". `openclaw update repair` exits 1 with "Plugin cohort recovery belongs to a different installation." Settling that stranded record is a separate follow-up at the recovery-admission owner; it is described under "Not proven".

## Why This Change Was Made

**Root cause, proven in a real cell with a resolve/spawn trace.**
- A pnpm package that an earlier OpenClaw update installed lives in its group's project-local virtual store: `global/v11/<group>/node_modules/.pnpm/openclaw@…`. Activating the next version moves that group into the transaction backup, so the running updater's own `dist` disappears.
- Work started inside the update loads workers through the retained-runtime generation, an AsyncLocalStorage binding to a retained copy. Two process-wide owners start workers from detached or earlier async contexts and still resolved them from the installed package:
  - the state lease heartbeat carrier (`runInDetachedAsyncContext`);
  - the file-log worker pool, whose URL was resolved at startup.
- The trace shows `new Worker(…/dist/state/openclaw-state-lease-heartbeat.worker.js)` and `…/dist/logging/logger-file.worker.js` from the removed store, then `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. The plugin lifecycle lease was lost ("First failure: plugin lifecycle lease core:plugin-lifecycle/global was lost … Cannot find module"). The command then unwound with the run's own unfinished recovery record.

**Which installs it hits.**
- **First update after the user's own `pnpm add -g`:** passes. That package lives in pnpm's shared `store/v11/links`, which activation does not move.
- **Every later pnpm update:** fails, on pnpm 12 and on 11.28.
- **npm:** passes, because the new package lands at the same path. Those detached workers then silently load the new version's worker files; with this change they load the retained copy, so the code matches.

**Not the cause.** `completeUpdateCommandRun` and `assertNoPendingUpdateRecovery` are not where it fails. CLI runs never get `completionOwner: "gateway-restart"`. The own-record refusal is the unwind's response to a genuine mid-activation failure; it is a consequence, not the cause. The recovery admission rule is unchanged, so an earlier run's unfinished recovery is still refused as today.

**Fix.** While the retained-runtime generation is bound, it also registers a process-wide resolver. `createCpuTrackedWorker`, through which every tracked worker spawn passes, applies it. An async-context binding still takes precedence, and outside an update that retained its runtime nothing changes. A URL the generation has already produced is final, so a worker captured in scope and then spawned is resolved once. The first CI run had shown a Bun-shard timeout in the heartbeat generation test, whose wrapping resolver imported itself when applied twice; the second commit fixes that, with a regression test that fails without it. `WorkerCpuHandle` and `WorkerMemoryMessage` move to `worker-cpu-types.ts` to keep `worker-cpu.ts` within its line cap. No stored field, config or schema changes.

## Evidence

Real cells used current-main builds A (`2026.11.20-beta.1`), B and C, built from `e17201c` (which includes a5779119b5f), plus fixed builds F1 and F2 built from this change. Each build has its own version; nothing was relabelled. The Gateway ran as a managed service under a busy 256 MiB write load.

| Cell | Second update (driven by an updater a previous update installed) | Run recorded | Raw logs |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Red**, pnpm 12.21: A → B → C (base) | B → C **exit 1 `update-recovery-pending`**; Gateway serves beta.3 | `running` / `verifying`, recovery set "ambiguous" | [log 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203458#issuecomment-7077866520); trace: [log 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203458#issuecomment-7077866765), [log 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203458#issuecomment-7077866984) |
| **Green**, pnpm 12.21: A → F1 → F2 | F1 → F2 **exit 0 `ok`**; Gateway serves beta.5 | `succeeded` | [log 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203458#issuecomment-7077867239), [log 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203458#issuecomment-7077867443), [log 3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203458#issuecomment-7077867689) |
| **Green**, pnpm 11.28.13: A → F1 → F2 | F1 → F2 exit 0 `ok` | `succeeded` | [log 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203458#issuecomment-7077867917), [log 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203458#issuecomment-7077868163), [log 3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203458#issuecomment-7077868445) |
| **npm**, unchanged: A → F1 → F2 | exit 0 `ok` | `succeeded` | [log 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203458#issuecomment-7077868688), [log 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203458#issuecomment-7077868937), [log 3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203458#issuecomment-7077869179) |
| Base npm control: A → B → C | exit 0 `ok` | `succeeded` | [log 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203458#issuecomment-7077869375), [log 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203458#issuecomment-7077869575) |

Unit regression at the owner, in `src/infra/runtime-worker-generation.test.ts`:
- **Setup:** a process owner created before the generation starts a real worker from its own async context after the installed script was deleted.
- **Green:** it loads the retained copy.
- **Red:** without the change it fails with the same "Cannot find module".
- **Negative control:** after the generation settles, the same owner loads the installed path again.

Other checks: the touched and adjacent tests pass (`worker-cpu`, worker-store generation, the Gateway owner heartbeat, state lease acquisition, update-restart module outcome, eager import closure). So do `pnpm tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test`, both cycle checks and the baseline ratchets.

Recordings (cell log live, then a summary from the raw files):

Green, pnpm 12, A → F1 → F2:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/afc69743-e42a-4d8f-8563-8e2ebd0f2099

The base failure with the resolve/spawn trace:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/89bbef7d-6a8b-4874-9c6a-9201fcd206c7

Base B → C, then the blocked later updates:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5b7096dd-fa57-4f6b-b41e-cb8e129a2f70

The raw cell logs are posted as PR comments and linked in the table above. Each comment holds the harness log and the full stderr and JSON stdout of the second update. The red cell adds `openclaw update status` after the failure, and the other cells add the final `openclaw update status --json` run record. The trace cell adds the resolve/spawn trace showing both missing worker paths and `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. No lines were cut; no line matched the host-identity scan.

## Cherry-pick for the release lines

On `release/2026.11.7` (#203401) and `release/2026.11.10` (#201740) the same change applies as two commits (`7413c6d` plus `d499c95` on 2026.11.7; `1d30fa2` plus `66e2acd` on 2026.11.10), without the type move, because `worker-cpu.ts` is under its cap there. The tests and `tsgo:core` pass on both.

## Not proven

- Bun installs and Windows.
- **Not fixed: an install already stuck by an unfixed build.** Its stranded record (`running`/`verifying` with a successful recorded verification, recovery set "ambiguous", owned by a removed store path) refuses every later update, and `openclaw update repair` refuses it as "a different installation". Clearing it automatically needs the recovery-admission and reconciliation owner to settle a run whose driver is gone, whose installation root no longer exists and whose verification succeeded. That changes an admission rule, so it is left for a decision. The manual way out is not verified yet.
- `autoreview` does not run on this machine.
